# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Dabour_2026_doxorubicin"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Dabour_2026_doxorubicin"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1111/cts.70595> (open access)
* Upstream doxorubicin PK and NT-proBNP model: Liang et al. 2016,
  <https://doi.org/10.1111/bcp.12989>

Dabour 2026 extended the authors' earlier doxorubicin PK / NT-proBNP model
(Liang 2016) with a model for growth differentiation factor 15 (GDF15). The
doxorubicin and doxorubicinol PK and the NT-proBNP layer were translated into
Monolix "without changes in PK model structure and population parameters"
(Dabour 2026, Methods), and the GDF15 layer was then estimated sequentially
with the individual PK parameters as regressors. The authors simulated all four
outputs together, so the packaged model carries the whole integrated system:

* doxorubicin: three-compartment disposition, short IV infusion;
* doxorubicinol: one compartment, formed from the doxorubicin central
  compartment; Liang 2016 estimated its clearance and volume divided by the
  unidentified fraction metabolized (`CL/fm`, `V/fm`);
* NT-proBNP: indirect response with five transit compartments, production
  stimulated linearly by the doxorubicin concentration (Liang 2016);
* GDF15: indirect response with four transit compartments, production
  stimulated by an Emax function of the doxorubicin concentration, baseline
  dependent on cumulative doxorubicin dose and BMI (Dabour 2026).

```{r model}
mod <- readModelDb("Dabour_2026_doxorubicin")
mod_ui <- rxode2::rxode2(mod)
```

# Population

Seventeen women aged 28-58 years (median 45) with stage I-III breast cancer
receiving adjuvant doxorubicin 60 mg/m^2 plus cyclophosphamide 600 mg/m^2
every 14 days for four cycles, enrolled in a randomized crossover study of
enalapril co-administration (Blaes 2015). Each woman contributed two
consecutive cycles, at different points of her regimen: 1, 4, 16 and 13
subject-cycles were sampled at cycles 1, 2, 3 and 4 (cumulative doxorubicin
60, 120, 180 and 240 mg/m^2). Median weight 65.3 kg (54.5-140.4), BMI 25.3
kg/m^2 (21.5-53.0), BSA 1.71 m^2 (1.60-2.50) (Dabour 2026 Table 1). Samples
were taken before and 0.5, 1, 2, 3, 4, 24 and 48 h after the end of the
doxorubicin infusion; 271 GDF15 concentrations were modelled.

```{r population}
str(mod()$population)
```

# Source trace

Every `ini()` value carries an in-file comment pointing to its source. The
doxorubicin, doxorubicinol and NT-proBNP values are the Liang 2016 final
estimates, which Dabour 2026 held fixed; they are wrapped in `fixed()`.

| Parameter | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `lcl` (CL, L/h) | 54.2 | Liang 2016 Table 2 |
| `lvc` (Vc, L) | 16.9 | Liang 2016 Table 2 |
| `lq` (Q2, L/h) | 66.1 | Liang 2016 Table 2 |
| `lvp` (V2, L) | 1650 | Liang 2016 Table 2 |
| `lq2` (Q3, L/h) | 23.4 | Liang 2016 Table 2 |
| `lvp2` (V3, L) | 61.8 | Liang 2016 Table 2 |
| `lcle_doxol` (CL_doxol/fm, L/h) | 106 | Liang 2016 Table 2 |
| `lvc_doxol` (V_doxol/fm, L) | 1880 | Liang 2016 Table 2 |
| `lkin_ntprobnp` (kin0, pg/mL/h) | 110 | Liang 2016 Table 3 |
| `lkout_ntprobnp` (kout, 1/h) | 1.66 (fixed in source) | Liang 2016 Table 3 |
| `lslope_ntprobnp` (beta, L/mg) | 115 | Liang 2016 Table 3, Equation 3 |
| `lmtt_ntprobnp` (MTT, h) | 34.7 | Liang 2016 Table 3, Equation 2 (`ktr = 5 / MTT`) |
| `lktr_gdf15` (Ktr, 1/h) | 0.851 | Dabour 2026 Table 2 |
| `lrbase_gdf15` (R0, pg/mL) | 744.866 | Dabour 2026 Table 2 |
| `lkout_gdf15` (Kout, 1/h) | 1.012 | Dabour 2026 Table 2 |
| `lemax_gdf15` (Emax) | 16.837 | Dabour 2026 Table 2 |
| `lec50_gdf15` (EC50, ug/mL) | 0.0385 | Dabour 2026 Table 2 |
| `e_dose_doxorubicin_cum_mgm2_rbase_gdf15` | 0.352 | Dabour 2026 Table 2 (beta1), Equation 4 |
| `e_bmi_rbase_gdf15` | 0.956 | Dabour 2026 Table 2 (beta2), Equation 4 |
| IIV CL, Vc, Q2, V2 | 8.33, 10.5, 15.4, 26.7 %CV | Liang 2016 Table 2 |
| IIV CL/fm, V/fm (doxorubicinol) | 18.5, 37.3 %CV | Liang 2016 Table 2 |
| IOV CL; CL/fm, V/fm | 3.86; 11.9, 9.39 %CV | Liang 2016 Table 2 |
| IIV kin0, beta, MTT; IOV kin0 | 48.5, 73.9, 38.8; 27.8 %CV | Liang 2016 Table 3 |
| IIV R0; IOV R0 | 31.72; 11.04 %CV | Dabour 2026 Table 2 |
| IIV Kout, EC50; correlation | 48.86, 59.79 %CV; -0.821 | Dabour 2026 Table 2 |
| Doxorubicin RUV | 8.73% proportional + 0.60 ng/mL additive | Liang 2016 Table 2 |
| Doxorubicinol RUV | 14.9% proportional | Liang 2016 Table 2 |
| NT-proBNP RUV | 23.8% proportional | Liang 2016 Table 3 |
| GDF15 RUV | 0.156 proportional | Dabour 2026 Table 2 |
| GDF15 ODEs and steady-state initial conditions | -- | Dabour 2026 Equations 1-2, Figure 1C |
| GDF15 baseline covariate model | -- | Dabour 2026 Equation 4 |
| NT-proBNP ODEs, `kin = kin0 * (1 + beta * Cdox)` | -- | Liang 2016 Equations 1-3, Figure 1B |
| Doxorubicinol formation from the doxorubicin central compartment | -- | Liang 2016 Figure 1A; Dabour 2026 Figure 1A |

Variances are `omega^2 = log(CV^2 + 1)`, the inverse of the CV formula both
papers print under their parameter tables. The covariance of the Kout and
EC50 etas is `-0.821 * sqrt(0.2141 * 0.3056) = -0.2100`.

# Typical-patient profiles

Typical-value simulation of one 60 mg/m^2 dose (15-minute infusion) in a
patient with BSA 1.71 m^2 and BMI 25.3 kg/m^2 at each cycle of the regimen.
This mirrors the deterministic EBE simulation of Dabour 2026 (Figure S4),
which reported a median GDF15 Tmax of 8.8 h (range 7.9-9.5 h) and an
NT-proBNP Tmax of 34.8 h (13.2-49.8 h) after the end of the infusion.

```{r typical}
tinf <- 0.25
bsa_typ <- 1.71
obs_times <- c(seq(0, 5, by = 0.05), seq(5.1, 120, by = 0.1)) + tinf

typ_events <- bind_rows(lapply(1:4, function(cyc) {
  bind_rows(
    data.frame(
      id = cyc, time = 0, evid = 1L, amt = 60 * bsa_typ,
      rate = 60 * bsa_typ / tinf, cmt = "central", dvid = NA_integer_
    ),
    data.frame(
      id = cyc, time = obs_times, evid = 0L, amt = 0, rate = 0,
      cmt = "central", dvid = 1L
    )
  ) |>
    mutate(OCC = 1L, BMI = 25.3, DOSE_DOXORUBICIN_CUM_MGM2 = 60 * cyc)
}))

typ <- rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod_ui), typ_events, returnType = "data.frame") |>
  mutate(
    cycle = factor(id, labels = paste0("Cycle ", 1:4, " (", 60 * (1:4), " mg/m^2)")),
    tpi = time - tinf
  )

tmax_typ <- typ |>
  group_by(cycle) |>
  summarise(
    gdf15_base = first(gdf15),
    gdf15_max = max(gdf15),
    tmax_gdf15 = tpi[which.max(gdf15)],
    ntprobnp_max = max(ntprobnp),
    tmax_ntprobnp = tpi[which.max(ntprobnp)],
    .groups = "drop"
  )
knitr::kable(tmax_typ, digits = 1)
```

```{r typical-check}
# The typical-value Tmax must fall inside the range of the 17 patients'
# EBE-simulated Tmax (Dabour 2026 Results); both sides are deterministic.
stopifnot(
  all(tmax_typ$tmax_gdf15 >= 7.9 & tmax_typ$tmax_gdf15 <= 9.5),
  all(tmax_typ$tmax_ntprobnp >= 13.2 & tmax_typ$tmax_ntprobnp <= 49.8)
)
```

```{r typical-plot, fig.cap = "Typical GDF15 and NT-proBNP profiles after one doxorubicin dose at each cycle; compare Dabour 2026 Figure S4."}
typ |>
  select(tpi, cycle, `GDF15 (pg/mL)` = gdf15, `NT-proBNP (pg/mL)` = ntprobnp) |>
  pivot_longer(-c(tpi, cycle)) |>
  ggplot(aes(tpi, value, colour = cycle)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~name, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "Time after end of infusion (h)", y = NULL, colour = NULL) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

# Virtual crossover cohort

A virtual cohort reproduces the study design: each subject receives two
consecutive cycles 14 days apart, starting at cycle 1, 2 or 3 in the 1 : 3 : 13
proportions of the enrolled patients (Liang 2016 Results). The study's BSA and
BMI distributions are right-skewed (BSA median 1.71 m^2, interquartile range
1.70-1.99, range 1.60-2.50; BMI median 25.3 kg/m^2, interquartile range
23.5-28.1, range 21.5-53.0; Dabour 2026 Table 1 and Table S1), so each is drawn
from the piecewise-linear quantile function through those five published
points. The occasion indicator and the
cumulative dose switch to the second cycle 24 h before its dose, after the
first cycle's response has resolved, so the second baseline is at its new
steady state when the dose is given.

```{r cohort}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20260513)
set.seed(20260513)
n_sub <- 150
first_cycle <- sample(1:3, n_sub, replace = TRUE, prob = c(1, 3, 13) / 17)
subj <- data.frame(
  id = seq_len(n_sub),
  first_cycle = first_cycle,
  BSA = approx(c(0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1), c(1.60, 1.70, 1.71, 1.99, 2.50), xout = runif(n_sub))$y,
  BMI = approx(c(0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1), c(21.5, 23.5, 25.3, 28.1, 53.0), xout = runif(n_sub))$y
)

t_switch <- 312
t_second <- 336
cycle_obs <- c(0, seq(0.5, 4, by = 0.5), seq(5, 48, by = 1)) + tinf

cohort_events <- bind_rows(
  subj |> mutate(time = 0, evid = 1L),
  subj |> mutate(time = t_second, evid = 1L),
  tidyr::crossing(subj, time = c(0, cycle_obs, t_switch, t_second + c(0, cycle_obs))) |>
    mutate(evid = 0L)
) |>
  mutate(
    amt = ifelse(evid == 1L, 60 * BSA, 0),
    rate = ifelse(evid == 1L, 60 * BSA / tinf, 0),
    cmt = "central",
    dvid = ifelse(evid == 0L, 1L, NA_integer_),
    OCC = ifelse(time < t_switch, 1L, 2L),
    DOSE_DOXORUBICIN_CUM_MGM2 = 60 * (first_cycle + OCC - 1L)
  ) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid)) |>
  select(id, time, evid, amt, rate, cmt, dvid, OCC, BMI, DOSE_DOXORUBICIN_CUM_MGM2)

cohort <- rxSolve(mod_ui, cohort_events, returnType = "data.frame",
  keep = c("OCC", "DOSE_DOXORUBICIN_CUM_MGM2"))

cohort <- cohort |>
  filter(time != t_switch) |>
  mutate(
    tpi = ifelse(OCC == 1L, time - tinf, time - t_second - tinf),
    dose_group = ifelse(DOSE_DOXORUBICIN_CUM_MGM2 <= 120, "60-120 mg/m^2", "180-240 mg/m^2")
  )
```

The plot below summarises the simulated GDF15 profiles over the first 48 h of
each cycle by cumulative-dose group, with the 5th, 50th and 95th percentiles
of individual predictions plus proportional residual error, for comparison
with the pcVPC of Dabour 2026 Figure 4B (observed medians of roughly
5000-6000 pg/mL at 24-48 h in the 180-240 mg/m^2 group).

```{r vpc, fig.cap = "Simulated GDF15 by cumulative doxorubicin dose group (median and 90% interval); compare Dabour 2026 Figures 3B and 4B."}
gdf15_sd <- 0.156
vpc_dat <- cohort |>
  filter(tpi >= 0) |>
  mutate(gdf15_obs = gdf15 * (1 + gdf15_sd * rnorm(n()))) |>
  group_by(dose_group, tpi) |>
  summarise(
    p05 = quantile(gdf15_obs, 0.05),
    p50 = median(gdf15_obs),
    p95 = quantile(gdf15_obs, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(dose_group = factor(dose_group, levels = c("60-120 mg/m^2", "180-240 mg/m^2")))

ggplot(vpc_dat, aes(tpi)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = p05, ymax = p95), fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_line(aes(y = p50), colour = "steelblue4") +
  scale_y_log10() +
  facet_wrap(~dose_group) +
  labs(x = "Time after end of infusion (h)", y = "GDF15 (pg/mL)") +
  theme_bw()
```

```{r vpc-check}
gdf15_24h <- vpc_dat |>
  filter(abs(tpi - 24) < 1e-6)
knitr::kable(gdf15_24h, digits = 0, caption = "Simulated GDF15 percentiles 24 h after infusion (pg/mL).")
# Centre-of-distribution check: a mis-scaled Emax, EC50 or baseline moves the
# 24-h median by far more than the band below, which brackets the observed
# median of about 6000 pg/mL in Dabour 2026 Figure 4B.
stopifnot(
  with(gdf15_24h, p50[dose_group == "180-240 mg/m^2"] > 4000),
  with(gdf15_24h, p50[dose_group == "180-240 mg/m^2"] < 9000)
)
```

# NCA of doxorubicin and doxorubicinol

The parent study reported non-compartmental doxorubicin and doxorubicinol
exposure (Dabour 2026 Supporting Information, section 3): mean AUC0-inf of
1167.7 and 1185.6 h*ng/mL for doxorubicin and 1056.3 and 1040.0 h*ng/mL for
doxorubicinol, without and with enalapril. The first cycle of each virtual
subject is sampled at the study times (before the infusion and 0.5, 1, 2, 3, 4,
24 and 48 h after it ends) and analysed the same way.

```{r nca}
nca_times <- c(0, c(0.5, 1, 2, 3, 4, 24, 48) + tinf)
pk_conc <- cohort |>
  filter(OCC == 1L, time %in% nca_times) |>
  mutate(treatment = "DOX 60 mg/m^2") |>
  select(id, time, treatment, Cc, Cc_doxol) |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc))
pk_dose <- cohort_events |>
  filter(evid == 1L, time == 0) |>
  mutate(treatment = "DOX 60 mg/m^2") |>
  select(id, time, treatment, amt)

nca_one <- function(conc_col) {
  conc <- pk_conc |>
    select(id, time, treatment, conc = all_of(conc_col))
  o_conc <- PKNCAconc(conc, conc ~ time | treatment + id)
  o_dose <- PKNCAdose(pk_dose, amt ~ time | treatment + id)
  intervals <- data.frame(start = 0, end = Inf, aucinf.obs = TRUE, cmax = TRUE, half.life = TRUE)
  pk.nca(PKNCAdata(o_conc, o_dose, intervals = intervals))
}
nca_dox <- nca_one("Cc")
nca_doxol <- nca_one("Cc_doxol")

mean_auc <- function(res, analyte) {
  as.data.frame(res) |>
    filter(PPTESTCD == "aucinf.obs") |>
    group_by(treatment, PPTESTCD) |>
    summarise(PPORRES = mean(PPORRES, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
    mutate(treatment = analyte)
}
sim_auc <- bind_rows(
  mean_auc(nca_dox, "Doxorubicin"),
  mean_auc(nca_doxol, "Doxorubicinol")
)
ref_auc <- data.frame(
  treatment = c("Doxorubicin", "Doxorubicinol"),
  aucinf.obs = c(1167.7, 1056.3)
)
nca_tbl <- ncaComparisonTable(
  sim_auc, ref_auc,
  by = "treatment",
  units = c(aucinf.obs = "h*ng/mL")
)
nca_tbl |>
  rename("Analyte" = treatment) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Mean AUC0-inf: simulated cycle 1 vs the parent study (without enalapril).")
```

Doxorubicin exposure agrees closely. The simulated doxorubicinol AUC is about
15% below the parent study's mean. The model cannot exceed `dose / (CL/fm)`
(about 970 h*ng/mL for a 60 mg/m^2 dose at BSA 1.71 m^2), so the gap is a
property of the Liang 2016 metabolite model rather than of the simulation:
Liang 2016 reports that doxorubicinol concentrations above 25 ng/mL were
under-predicted (their Figure 2C) and that neither an extra metabolite
compartment nor a log transformation removed the bias. The published
parameters are kept as printed.

```{r nca-summary}
as.data.frame(nca_dox) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "half.life")) |>
  group_by(PPTESTCD) |>
  summarise(median = median(PPORRES, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Simulated doxorubicin Cmax (ng/mL, at the first sample 0.5 h after infusion) and terminal half-life (h, from samples to 48 h).")
```

# Day-14 GDF15 risk stratification

Dabour 2026 simulated 1000 virtual patients at cumulative doses of 60, 120,
180 and 240 mg/m^2 and classified the Day-14 GDF15 concentration (the last
day before the next cycle) as low (< 1200 pg/mL), moderate (1200-1800 pg/mL)
or high (> 1800 pg/mL) cardiovascular risk: 64.7%, 26.6% and 8.7% overall
(Figure 6B). Height and weight were drawn from a truncated bivariate normal
fitted to the study data, whose mean and covariance the paper does not
print. Here they are reconstructed from the virtual-cohort medians and
interquartile ranges in Table S1 (height 165.1 cm, 159.0-170.7; weight 69.27
kg, 62.28-76.12), with a height-weight correlation of 0.59 chosen so that the
derived BMI interquartile range matches Table S1 (23.33-27.44 kg/m^2).
Simulation is 200 patients per dose arm, with between-subject and
inter-occasion variability and no residual error.

```{r pta}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20260514)
set.seed(20260514)
n_arm <- 200
arms <- c(60, 120, 180, 240)
ht_mu <- 165.1
wt_mu <- 69.27
ht_sd <- (170.7 - 159.0) / 1.349
wt_sd <- (76.12 - 62.28) / 1.349
rho_hw <- 0.59
z1 <- rnorm(n_arm * length(arms))
z2 <- rho_hw * z1 + sqrt(1 - rho_hw^2) * rnorm(n_arm * length(arms))
pta_subj <- data.frame(
  id = seq_len(n_arm * length(arms)),
  DOSE_DOXORUBICIN_CUM_MGM2 = rep(arms, each = n_arm),
  height = ht_mu + ht_sd * z1,
  weight = wt_mu + wt_sd * z2
) |>
  mutate(
    BMI = weight / (height / 100)^2,
    BSA = 0.007184 * weight^0.425 * height^0.725
  )

pta_events <- bind_rows(
  pta_subj |> mutate(time = 0, evid = 1L, amt = 60 * BSA, rate = 60 * BSA / tinf, dvid = NA_integer_),
  pta_subj |> mutate(time = 14 * 24 + tinf, evid = 0L, amt = 0, rate = 0, dvid = 1L)
) |>
  mutate(cmt = "central", OCC = 1L) |>
  arrange(id, time) |>
  select(id, time, evid, amt, rate, cmt, dvid, OCC, BMI, DOSE_DOXORUBICIN_CUM_MGM2)

pta <- rxSolve(mod_ui, pta_events, returnType = "data.frame",
  keep = "DOSE_DOXORUBICIN_CUM_MGM2") |>
  mutate(
    risk = cut(gdf15, c(-Inf, 1200, 1800, Inf),
      labels = c("Low", "Moderate", "High"), right = FALSE)
  )

risk_overall <- pta |>
  count(risk) |>
  mutate(simulated_pct = 100 * n / sum(n), published_pct = c(64.7, 26.6, 8.7))
knitr::kable(risk_overall, digits = 1, caption = "Day-14 GDF15 risk categories, all dose arms (published: Dabour 2026 Figure 6B).")

pta |>
  count(risk, DOSE_DOXORUBICIN_CUM_MGM2) |>
  group_by(risk) |>
  mutate(pct_of_category = 100 * n / sum(n)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  select(risk, DOSE_DOXORUBICIN_CUM_MGM2, pct_of_category) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = DOSE_DOXORUBICIN_CUM_MGM2, values_from = pct_of_category) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Share of each risk category by cumulative dose (mg/m^2), percent; Dabour 2026 Figure 6B reports 34.6% of the low-risk group at 60 mg/m^2 and 48.3% of the high-risk group at 240 mg/m^2.")
```

```{r pta-check}
# Category fractions are centre-of-distribution statistics of 800 subjects
# (Monte Carlo SE about 1-2 points); the bands catch a mis-scaled covariate
# exponent or baseline without depending on which subjects land in the tails.
stopifnot(
  with(risk_overall, simulated_pct[risk == "Low"] > 50),
  with(risk_overall, simulated_pct[risk == "High"] < 16)
)
```

```{r pta-plot, fig.cap = "Simulated Day-14 GDF15 by cumulative doxorubicin dose with the 1200 and 1800 pg/mL risk thresholds; compare Dabour 2026 Figure 6A."}
ggplot(pta, aes(factor(DOSE_DOXORUBICIN_CUM_MGM2), gdf15)) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.2, alpha = 0.3, colour = "steelblue") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = c(1200, 1800), linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(x = "Cumulative dose (mg/m^2)", y = "GDF15 at Day 14 post infusion (pg/mL)") +
  theme_bw()
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Integrated model in one file.** The doxorubicin, doxorubicinol and
  NT-proBNP layers are Liang 2016's final estimates, which Dabour 2026
  carried unchanged and simulated together with the new GDF15 layer. They are
  encoded as `fixed()` because Dabour 2026 did not re-estimate them.
* **NT-proBNP units.** Liang 2016 Table 3 labels the production rate in
  ng/mL/h, but the NT-proBNP data (Liang 2016 Figure 3C) are in pg/mL and
  `kin0 / kout = 110 / 1.66 = 66` matches the observed baseline only in pg/mL.
  The model uses pg/mL/h. The Liang 2016 Results text quotes a typical
  `kin0` of 97.4; the table value 110 is used.
* **Units of the drug effects.** Both biomarker effects use the doxorubicin
  concentration in mg/L (= ug/mL), the unit of the GDF15 EC50 (0.0385 ug/mL).
  Liang 2016 prints the NT-proBNP slope as 115 L/ug; with the concentration in
  mg/L this slope reproduces the roughly four-fold NT-proBNP rise at 24-48 h
  seen in Liang 2016 Figure 3C, whereas a per-ug/L slope would predict a rise
  of several hundred-fold, so the slope is read as L/mg.
* **Doxorubicinol formation.** The fraction metabolized is not identifiable;
  the doxorubicinol state holds the amount divided by `fm`, fed by the whole
  doxorubicin clearance and eliminated at `(CL/fm) / (V/fm)`, so the
  concentration equals that of the published reparameterization.
* **Residual error forms.** Liang 2016 used NONMEM with a combined additive
  plus proportional doxorubicin error; the nlmixr2 `add() + prop()` form
  (variances summed) is assumed.
* **Inter-occasion variability.** rxode2 has no occasion level, so each IOV
  term is expanded into two etas selected by `OCC` (the two study cycles). The
  occasion etas are not mu-referenced, and rxode2 warns about that on every
  solve; this has no effect on simulation.
* **Covariate column.** The cumulative doxorubicin dose through the current
  cycle is carried in the `DOSE_DOXORUBICIN_CUM_MGM2` column. It includes the
  current cycle (60 mg/m^2 at cycle 1), unlike `PRIOR_ANTHRACYCLINE_DOSE`.
* **Infusion duration.** Simulations use the study's intended 15-minute
  infusion (Liang 2016); Dabour 2026 does not state the duration it simulated.
* **Risk-stratification cohort.** The truncated bivariate normal of height and
  weight is not printed; the reconstruction above matches the Table S1
  medians and interquartile ranges but not necessarily its tails or
  truncation limits. Whether the published Day-14 simulation included the
  inter-occasion variability of R0 is not stated; it is included here. The
  arms are equal in size, as Figure 6A suggests.
* **Doxorubicin AUC.** The model's dose / CL is about 1890 h*ng/mL for a
  60 mg/m^2 dose at BSA 1.71 m^2; an NCA truncated at 48 h with extrapolation
  from the late samples recovers a smaller value, which is how the study's NCA
  was done. The comparison above applies the same sampling to the simulation.
* No errata were found for either paper (checked 2026-11-13).
